draft.title: Change and continuity in Russia
card: In 1896 Russia was ruled by a tsar with almost unlimited power. By 1927 the tsar was gone, and the Communist Party ruled in the name of workers and peasants.
Land had passed to the peasants, and the Soviets and the party replaced the old tsarist government and its nobles.
Power stayed in the hands of a few, with no free elections and little room for opponents. The Tsar's secret police, the Okhrana, was followed by the Cheka.
Historians weigh both. The rulers and the ideas had changed, but some of the methods of control stayed the same.
draft.remember: The tsar was replaced, but one-party rule and secret police echoed the old pattern of power.

a.q: Which is an example of continuity between tsarist and Bolshevik Russia?
opts: A secret police force that watched and punished opponents
A tsar who ruled with almost unlimited power
Land that was owned mainly by nobles
A ruling class made up of the old nobility
a.why: The Okhrana under the tsar and the Cheka under the Bolsheviks both policed opponents. The other options describe tsarist Russia, which had ended by 1927, so they show change, not continuity.
a.clue: Look for something that existed under both the tsar and the Bolsheviks.

b.q: A student argues that Russia in 1927 had changed little since 1896. Which fact best supports a claim of change, not continuity?
opts: The tsar had been removed and a party ruled in his place
Opponents could not freely stand in elections
A secret police force still arrested political critics
Power was held by a small group at the top
b.why: Removing the tsar and replacing him with party rule is a real change in who held power. The other three show the same old pattern of control, which is continuity, even though the secret police had a new name.
b.clue: Pick the fact that shows something different from 1896.

a.best: A secret police force that watched and punished opponents

b.best: The tsar had been removed and a party ruled in his place
